title: 5-minute planning
examples: Should I write everything I think of first?
How long should my plan take?
Is it better to plan or just start writing?

explain.say: When you start writing, you should always plan first.
Brainstorming means writing down every idea you have about your topic.
Next, you must order those ideas so they make sense together.
A paragraph plan helps you structure each single section clearly.
For example, if you write about dogs, you might plan one paragraph for play.

items: Topic Sentence | Supporting Detail 1 | Concluding Sentence
Dogs love to run | Fetch is fun | They need exercise

explain.say: In real life, when you write a report, you plan before you write it.

faq.q: Do I have to write down every single word in my plan?
faq.a: No, you only need key ideas and the order of your points. You are planning, not writing the essay.

faq.q: What is the difference between brainstorming and outlining?
faq.a: Brainstorming is free-flowing ideas without order. Outlining takes those ideas and puts them in a specific sequence.

faq.q: If my topic is very simple, do I still need a plan?
faq.a: Yes, even simple topics benefit from planning. It keeps your writing focused and makes it stronger.
asks: Is planning only for big essays?
Do I need structure for short pieces?

faq.q: How long should my plan take me?
faq.a: It should take enough time to feel complete, but not so long that you lose your writing momentum. A few minutes is usually enough.
asks: Can I spend too long planning?

faq.q: What if I change my mind while writing?
faq.a: If you change your mind, your plan helps you see where the best place for the new idea is. You can adjust your order easily.
asks: Can I skip the plan if I get stuck?
How do I fix a plan mid-writing?

facts: Brainstorming generates a large quantity of ideas quickly.
Ordering points creates a logical flow for the reader.
A paragraph plan structures the topic sentence, details, and conclusion.
Planning helps maintain focus throughout the writing process.

quiz.say: Which stage involves writing down every idea without stopping to judge them?
quiz.why: Brainstorming is the initial stage for gathering all possible thoughts on a topic.

wrong.0: This step focuses only on the structure of one small section, not all ideas.
wrong.1: Drafting is the act of writing the full text, which happens after planning.
wrong.3: Ordering requires you to select and sequence the best ideas, which is a later step.

quiz.say: If your essay moves from causes to effects, what step are you completing?
quiz.why: Ordering means arranging your collected ideas into the most sensible sequence for your reader.

wrong.1: Brainstorming is about quantity of ideas, not their correct sequence.
wrong.2: This only organizes one small part, not the whole essay's flow.
wrong.3: Concluding is only the final part; ordering is the process leading up to it.

quiz.say: A plan that uses a Topic Sentence, Details, and a final thought is an example of:
quiz.why: This specific structure—topic, support, conclusion—is the definition of a paragraph plan.

wrong.0: Brainstorming would list many random ideas, not this structured format.
wrong.1: Ordering looks at the sequence between paragraphs, not the structure within one.
wrong.2: The conclusion is only the last part, not the plan for the whole paragraph.
